service.description: The names this node answers: its own host (webapp_http_host), each public-site host, the SMTP host (smtp_hostname), the XMPP domain, each terminate host of a pairing on an edge node, each name set up with ACME and each name with files in runtime/cert. For each: hostName, reasons (what makes it one of the names), found, and certificate when the HTTPS listener would serve one for it: pair (the files' name: the name, its wildcard or default), matchKind (exact, wildcard or default), file (under the runtime), layout (certbot, nginx-proxy or mkcert), acmeWritten, issuer, notAfter (millis), daysLeft and problem (why the files do not load). A name set up with ACME has acme: directoryUrl, contactEmail, renewing, statusId, lastAttemptDate, lastError, notAfter, setUpDate, ordering (this server is ordering it now) and shadowed (another tool's files for the name are served instead). Also listenPort (the HTTPS listener's port when it is bound), directoryUrl (acme_directory_url), stagingUrl (Let's Encrypt's staging directory) and challengePort.

Set a name up to get its certificate from an ACME authority, then order it on a thread of its own: the name's row shows the outcome (AcmeOrdering, then AcmeIssued or AcmeFailed with lastError), and the renewal job (renew_AcmeCertificates_daily) is started. First it checks that the name has an address in DNS and that a TLS connection to it on the challenge port (443) reaches this node, unless skipCheck. Refuses a name that is not a DNS name (badName), a directory URL that is not https (badDirectory), terms not agreed (termsNotAgreed), a contact that is not an email address (badContact), a runtime/cert/hostName/ directory another tool wrote (otherTool), and a failed check (checkFailed, with what was found). A name set up before takes the new authority, contact and terms, and renews again.

parameter.name: directoryUrl
parameter.description: The authority's directory; acme_directory_url when empty.

service.description: Order the certificate of a name set up with ACME again now, on a thread of its own. Refuses a name not set up (notSetUp) and one being ordered (ordering).
Stop renewing a name set up with ACME (renewing false), or renew it again (true). Its certificate stays until it runs out. Refuses a name not set up (notSetUp).

Forget a name set up with ACME: its rows, and its files in runtime/cert here now and on the other members of a cluster within a minute. Its HTTPS is refused then, unless another certificate covers it. The renewal job pauses with the last name. removed is false when the name was not set up.

The renewal job's service: renew, one after another, each name set up with ACME and renewing whose certificate is missing or has a third of its life left (30 days with no issue date), leaving out one being ordered and one that failed in the last six hours. One that fails is logged and the others go on. Never asks for a name not set up.
